Title: Preflight inventory and reconciliation
User story / technical objective: Before writing code, inventory what exists so IADM-07 reuses it and duplicates nothing.
Acceptance criteria: One-page report covering: branch and working-tree state; conventions of IADM-01, 02, 04, 05 and 06 (port, route prefix, permission-key naming, schema naming, migration style, FORCE row-level security style, demo-persona pattern, stale or runtime setting pattern); next free port after 8104 and route collision check against legacy /api/v1/admin/...; legacy adm07.* keys and any legacy security governance code with a REUSE/MOVE/NEW proposal (move, do not copy); how the existing shared identity and shared audit (audit.log_event) work, including failure behaviour; whether the shared audit has a read path for denial-type events and how the Audit tabs of IADM-05 and IADM-06 read it; whether a shared notification service exists; how a service caller is authenticated on the IADM-05 domain contract; whether RBAC has an Auditor audit-scope assignment (IADM-06 found none) and whether any college attribute exists; which demo institutes and personas already exist. Anything not found is written TBC. Confirms the DB target is the DEV Supabase project.
Build default or status: Read-only; no code or DB change

Title: IADM-07 service scaffold
User story / technical objective: Create IADM-07 as a separate deployable Java service following the conventions found in the preflight.
Acceptance criteria: Service starts; health endpoint answers; gateway route registered with no collision; exception handling and structured logging; no sensitive payload in logs; technical doc started. Port and route reported (blueprint proposes 8105 and /api/v1/iadm/07, confirmed or corrected by preflight).
Build default or status: Proposal only; preflight value wins

Title: Permission keys and role mapping
User story / technical objective: Define the IADM-07 permission keys and map them to the five roles that have an IADM-07 posture.
Acceptance criteria: Capabilities: view posture and indicators; read registers; write registers; approve standards and decide exceptions (Super Admin only); signal intake (service caller only); view reports; view audit evidence. Mapping: Super Admin (R01) manage all and sole approver; System Admin (R02) manage and triage, may propose, never approve or decide; Institution Admin (R03) own institute only, limited writes; College Admin (R04) view published standards and institute posture summary only; Auditor (R28) view only, no export. Names follow the convention (iadm07.*). No wildcard; no role outside R01, R02, R03, R04, R28 receives any key; each denial tested. Legacy adm07.* keys left untouched, mapping reported.
Build default or status: Key strings reported, not approved in advance

Title: Schema, tenant scoping and row-level security
User story / technical objective: Create IADM-07's own registers in DEV: security standards, signals, findings, risks, controls with per-institute assessments, evidence references, exceptions, alerts, enforcement-status records.
Acceptance criteria: Short own schema following the convention (blueprint proposes iadm07). Institute-scoped rows carry the institute; platform-level rows have none. FORCE row-level security on every table. No copies of other services' data, no audit table, no configuration or identity table. Evidence is stored as reference only (identifier or address, source, time), never a file payload. Rollback script included. Test: an institute cannot read another institute's rows; missing or mismatched tenant context fails closed.
Build default or status: Table and column names are a build proposal, reported at S0

Title: Shared audit integration
User story / technical objective: Write an audit event for every mutation through the existing shared audit function.
Acceptance criteria: Uses audit.log_event; no second audit store. Event holds actor, action, scope, record reference and correlation id, no sensitive content. If the audit event cannot be recorded, the mutation is refused and nothing is reported as successful. Test covers audit-unavailable.
Build default or status: If no reusable audit exists this is a blocker: report

Title: View platform security posture
User story / technical objective: As R01 Super Admin I can view platform-wide security posture within explicit platform scope.
Acceptance criteria: Posture overview shows the indicators platform-wide, the high-priority risks and links to the registers, with seeded figures. Stale or unavailable data is labelled and never shown as healthy. No wildcard access; audited.
Build default or status: None

Title: Manage security governance operations
User story / technical objective: As R02 System Admin I can manage permitted security governance operations without self-grant or unaudited changes.
Acceptance criteria: Can create and update findings, risks and alerts and operate triage; can propose standards and exceptions. Cannot approve or decide (403) and cannot change anyone's access. Every change audited; if audit is unavailable the change is refused.
Build default or status: None

Title: View published standards and institute posture summary
User story / technical objective: As R04 College Admin I can view only the security information exposed to my scope.
Acceptance criteria: Sees published standards and the institute posture summary (counts only). No individual finding, risk, signal or evidence detail; any such request returns 403. No create, update or delete control.
Build default or status: The blueprint's earlier wording 'college scope' is read as institute summary; college detail only if preflight proves a college attribute

Actor / role: System Admin (R02) proposes; Super Admin (R01) approves and publishes
Title: Propose, approve and publish a security standard
User story / technical objective: As R02 System Admin I can propose a security standard, and as R01 Super Admin I can approve and publish it.
Acceptance criteria: R02 drafts and submits for review; R01 (a different account from the author) approves; R01 publishes with effective and review dates. Published version is immutable; a change creates a new version and the old one becomes Superseded. R02 cannot approve or publish (403). Every step audited. Screen lets both personas do the work on seeded data.
Build default or status: This register is not IADM-02 configuration and not IADM-05 data policy

Actor / role: Super Admin (R01); System Admin (R02); Institution Admin (R03) own institute; College Admin (R04); Auditor (R28)
Title: View posture indicators within my scope
User story / technical objective: As any of these roles I can view the security posture indicators within my scope.
Acceptance criteria: R01, R02 and R28 see platform-wide; R03 sees own institute only; R04 sees summary-level counts only. Each indicator shows its stale state. Changing the DEMO ONLY stale threshold in the headed run makes the stale case show as stale, never healthy.
Build default or status: None

Title: Register lifecycle engine
User story / technical objective: One engine for the lifecycles of standards, findings, risks, controls, exceptions and alerts.
Acceptance criteria: Statuses and transitions exactly as the blueprint tables. Standard versions are immutable once published; a change creates a new Draft version. Author or requester and approver must be different accounts. R01 alone approves standards and decides exceptions. Allowed transitions are checked per role (R03 limited as in the finding and alert stories). Exceptions need a validity window; expiry is derived at read time so an expired exception stops applying without a scheduler. Invalid transitions return a clear refusal.
Build default or status: Expiry derived at read time (no new scheduler or infrastructure)

Title: Demo dataset and personas, grown each slice
User story / technical objective: Make every screen show real rows from the first slice.
Acceptance criteria: Reuse the existing IADM-01 demo institutes and the existing demo personas (Super Admin, System Admin, Institution Admin per demo institute, College Admin, Auditor); invent no institute IDs, user IDs or emails; follow the existing demo-persona pattern. DEMO ONLY rows: SEC-FIND-001, SEC-RISK-001, SEC-CTRL-001, SEC-ALERT-001, SEC-EXC-001, a published and review-due standard, an evidence-pending reference, a deliberately stale register case (SEC-SRC-STALE) and one deliberate empty case. Each later slice adds its own rows. Seeds idempotent and removable. No real personal data or real telemetry.
Build default or status: Severity labels are DEMO ONLY: Critical, High, Medium, Low; SLA values blank

Title: Posture indicator engine
User story / technical objective: Compute the nine approved posture indicators from IADM-07's own registers.
Acceptance criteria: Indicators: open findings by severity; overdue remediations (needs a recorded target date; none means not counted); controls by assessment status; pending exceptions; expiring exceptions; open alerts; evidence pending; standards due for review; stale-source indicator. Scope per role (platform, own institute, summary only). A register is stale when its last update exceeds the configurable DEMO ONLY runtime threshold or it cannot be read; stale or unavailable is never shown as healthy or zero. The threshold setting is built here and its value reported.
Build default or status: Threshold is DEMO ONLY; production policy OWNER-OPEN

Title: View and update own-institute posture
User story / technical objective: As R03 Institution Admin I can view and update only my institute's permitted security posture.
Acceptance criteria: Sees own institute posture, assigned findings, control gaps and alerts. May move assigned findings from Assigned to Remediation In Progress and to Pending Verification, attach an evidence reference, and acknowledge own alerts. May not mark Resolved, edit standards or control definitions, change platform data, or touch another institute (403, tested with a second institute). May request exceptions (see the exception story).
Build default or status: BUILD DEFAULT field and transition list; owner may overrule

Title: Review and triage signals
User story / technical objective: As R01 or R02 I can review and triage security and access signals.
Acceptance criteria: Signal list with severity, source, time and status (New, Acknowledged, Investigating, Closed). Triage changes audited. A signal can be turned into a finding or an alert. Source unavailable shows as stale or unavailable, never as 'no threats'. Denial-type audit events appear read-only only if preflight confirmed a shared-audit read path; otherwise omitted.
Build default or status: Denial-event display depends on preflight

Title: Track findings and remediation
User story / technical objective: As R01 or R02 I can track vulnerability findings and remediation evidence.
Acceptance criteria: Create, triage, assign, track and verify findings through Open, Triaged, Assigned, Remediation In Progress, Pending Verification, Resolved. Target date and evidence references recorded. Only R01 or R02 can mark Resolved, after a verification step. Overdue is shown only where a target date exists. Technical remediation is never performed or claimed by IADM-07.
Build default or status: None

Title: View policy enforcement status
User story / technical objective: As R01 or R02 I can view policy enforcement status reported by the actual enforcing services.
Acceptance criteria: Screen lists enforcement-status reports by control and service with report time, received through the intake endpoint or entered manually. A control with no recent report shows 'not reported' or 'unknown', never 'enforced'. IADM-07 enforces nothing.
Build default or status: No real enforcing service is wired in V1; demo reports come from the simulator

Actor / role: Super Admin (R01); System Admin (R02); Institution Admin (R03) own institute
Title: Acknowledge and track alerts
User story / technical objective: As R01 or R02, and R03 for own-institute alerts, I can acknowledge and track security alerts without depending on notification delivery.
Acceptance criteria: Alerts are in-app, with statuses Open, Acknowledged, Resolved. R03 sees and acknowledges only its own institute's alerts. Everything works with the notification service off; if a shared notification service exists it is best effort only.
Build default or status: None

Title: Submit a security signal
User story / technical objective: As an authenticated service caller I can submit a security signal through the intake endpoint.
Acceptance criteria: Accepted signal appears in the signal list as New with the source flagged DEMO ONLY. Unauthenticated call refused. Duplicate creates no second record; conflict is flagged for review. No external scanner, SIEM or agent is involved.
Build default or status: Simulator is DEMO ONLY

Title: Authenticated signal intake endpoint
User story / technical objective: Service-to-service endpoint through which approved services submit security signals and enforcement-status reports.
Acceptance criteria: Only an authenticated service caller (same method as the IADM-05 contract) is accepted; unknown or forged caller refused. Institute scope is validated, never trusted from the payload alone. Duplicate submissions (same correlation id) create no second record; a conflicting repeat is flagged for review. Records references only, no raw payload. Documented as versioned.
Build default or status: No Kafka, no outbox

Title: Signal intake simulator (DEMO ONLY)
User story / technical objective: A clearly labelled demo caller that plays a monitoring or enforcing service.
Acceptance criteria: Flagged DEMO ONLY in code, data and screen; uses the real intake endpoint like any caller; can send new, duplicate and conflicting signals and an enforcement-status report; can be disabled by one setting; touches no real service.
Build default or status: Real telemetry sources are OWNER-OPEN

Title: Track compliance controls and evidence
User story / technical objective: As R01 or R02 I can track compliance controls and evidence without asserting certification.
Acceptance criteria: DEMO ONLY control catalogue with a free-text framework field; per-institute assessment status through Not Assessed, Evidence Pending, In Review, Satisfied, Gap, Exception. Evidence is a reference only. No screen, report or export says an institute is compliant or certified. R03 can add evidence only for own-institute records and cannot edit control definitions.
Build default or status: Real frameworks are OWNER-OPEN

Title: Request a policy exception
User story / technical objective: As R03 or R02 I can request a policy exception.
Acceptance criteria: Request holds scope, rationale, linked control or finding and a mandatory validity window. R03 can request only for its own institute. Status Requested; requester cannot decide it. Audited.
Build default or status: Blueprint stories US-010 and US-016 were duplicates; split here into request (this row) and decision (US-016)

Title: Decide a policy exception
User story / technical objective: As R01 Super Admin I can decide a policy exception.
Acceptance criteria: R01 approves or rejects with rationale; the decider must be a different account from the requester; R02 and R03 cannot decide (403). Approved exceptions carry the expiry; when it passes, the exception shows Expired and no longer counts. Seeded pending and expiring examples exist.
Build default or status: R01 is the sole approver (owner may overrule)

Actor / role: Super Admin (R01); System Admin (R02); Institution Admin (R03) own institute; College Admin (R04); Auditor (R28)
Title: View control catalogue and evidence status
User story / technical objective: As any of these roles I can view the compliance control catalogue and evidence status within my scope.
Acceptance criteria: R01, R02 and R28 see all; R03 sees own-institute assessments; R04 sees summary counts only (per the role map); each row labelled DEMO ONLY. Missing evidence shows as pending, never satisfied.
Build default or status: R04 limited to counts to match the role map

Actor / role: Super Admin (R01); System Admin (R02); Institution Admin (R03) own institute; College Admin (R04); Auditor (R28)
Title: View security reports on screen
User story / technical objective: As any of these roles I can view security reports on screen within my scope.
Acceptance criteria: Report shows current counts by status and severity plus counts created and resolved per month, computed from IADM-07's own register timestamps; stale or partial labelled. No export control exists for any role. R03 own institute; R04 summary only.
Build default or status: Export deferred; trends come only from IADM-07's own register history

Title: Read-only security evidence
User story / technical objective: As R28 Auditor I can inspect security evidence read-only.
Acceptance criteria: Reads posture, registers, controls, evidence, reports and audit evidence platform-wide by default (reported at preflight whether an audit-scope assignment exists). Every create, update, approve, decide or export attempt returns 403. No export control shown.
Build default or status: The blueprint story says 'assigned scope'; the build default is platform-wide read-only

Actor / role: Super Admin (R01); System Admin (R02); Institution Admin (R03) own institute; Auditor (R28)
Title: Trace governance mutations through shared audit
User story / technical objective: As these roles I can trace security governance mutations through the shared audit.
Acceptance criteria: An Audit evidence screen lists the shared audit entries for IADM-07 mutations with actor, action, scope and correlation id, read-only, using the same read path as the IADM-05 and IADM-06 audit tabs. R03 sees own institute only. Audit unavailable shows 'unavailable' and the mutation was refused.
Build default or status: None

Title: Verify ownership boundaries are preserved
User story / technical objective: As R01 Super Admin I can verify that IADM-02, IADM-03, IADM-05 and IADM-08 ownership boundaries are preserved.
Acceptance criteria: Evidence: schema inventory shows only the register tables; no configuration, identity or audit table; IADM-07 cannot write a platform default or any permission or role; standards register separate from IADM-02 configuration and IADM-05 policy; no technical remediation or enforcement code. Documented with checks.
Build default or status: Verification story

Title: Verify isolation and role boundaries
User story / technical objective: As R01 or R02 I can verify tenant isolation, R04 view-only and R28 read-only enforcement.
Acceptance criteria: Tests and headed run show: Institution Admin of one institute cannot reach another's records; R04 and R28 mutations return 403 at API and screen; a role outside R01, R02, R03, R04, R28 is denied; row-level security enforced.
Build default or status: None

Title: Failure, isolation and role test suite
User story / technical objective: Automated tests for every row of the blueprint failure table and for role and tenant boundaries.
Acceptance criteria: Covers missing permission, cross-institute request, audit unavailable (mutation refused), signal source unavailable (stale, not secure), duplicate and conflicting signals, enforcement service unavailable (not claimed enforced), missing evidence (stays pending), notification outage (in-app unaffected), database or row-level-security denial. Role tests for R01, R02, R03 (two institutes), R04, R28 and one other role that must be denied. Log-leak check: no tokens, credentials or evidence content in logs.
Build default or status: None

Title: Evidence pack and close-out
User story / technical objective: Prove the work is done the way the owner defined done.
Acceptance criteria: Headed run for every persona (R01, R02, R03 for two institutes, R04, R28) showing real seeded rows on every screen; the faults filmed: audit unavailable, signal source stale, notification off, failed or invalid transition, self-approval refusal; test results; plain-language report; blueprint demo checklist ticked with evidence; decisions D1 to D16 with what the build assumed; table of all rows target versus actual; anything partial marked honestly; final git status.
Build default or status: None
